localChanges: chore: update core-requirement, civ1-world, civ1-unit, civ1-city-happiness, civ1-wonder and simple-ai-client

log: `civ1-city-happiness:city/cost/enhanced-by/Temple`: a Temple is enhanced by Mysticism. It only describes, for the civilopedia; `Rules/City/cost`'s table plays it (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).

The Worker's irrigation rule stays written by hand (it asks civ1-world's entries for the terrain). A describing entry, `civ1-unit:unit/action/improvement/Irrigation`, names its water condition for the civilopedia (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).

From the review: the Worker's irrigation rule refuses for other reasons too, so the describing entry is `civ1-unit:unit/action/improvement/Irrigation/water-nearby` rather than sharing the rule's id, and its condition's docs include a tile that is itself a River (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).
`civ1-wonder:wonder/enhanced-by/Oracle`: the Oracle is enhanced by Mysticism. It only describes, for the civilopedia; `Rules/City/cost` plays it (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).

`Requirements.ts` declares the entries: the terrains Irrigation, Mines, Roads and Railroads can go on (`where`), a road on a River needing Bridge Building, and a Railroad needing the Railroad advance and a Road. `registerRules` adds them to the game's `requirements`, which makes the `Available` rules from them with `Rules/TileImprovement/available`'s deriver: the same criteria, first in registration order as before, now named. A tile improvement can be built by any one of its rules, so each entry is one way to build it (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).
`getRules` still returns every rule, for rule registries without a game's `requirements`.

From the review: an entry without `where` now means any terrain, as core-requirement documents, rather than none; an entry needing `any` of its targets, or a target that is neither a tile improvement nor an advance, is refused rather than played wrongly; the docs say an advance is the working player's. A test shows a second Road isn't offered where there's one already (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).

`enhancedBy` says a subject works better while its targets are met (a Temple with Mysticism). It only describes: the owning package's rules play the effect, as an entry can't say by how much. The docs say what `where` is for (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).
docs: a comma the README lost

civ1-player 0.1.9 (f246542) keeps a civilization a client chose before the world was built. createClients() chooses one, so the Built rule no longer awaits the client and spawns its Settlers before simpleWorldLoader() resolves. The land exploration test then saw 9 tiles before its Warrior existed, failed before its clean-up, and left its client registered, so every later world gave that player Settlers too, among other tests' units.

Those meetings reached civ1-diplomacy's negotiation rules, which the suite still built with the pre-843d665 positional arguments, so the first negotiation threw ("reading 'register'"). A later failed .equal() on two Tiles then had mocha's reporter stringify the whole game graph for its diff, which ran out of memory.

No test wants the spawned Settlers (the four that met them removed them), so the start-tile rule is left out and removeSpawnedSettlers goes. civ1-diplomacy's rules get its Dependencies, and chai's showDiff is off so a failed comparison of game objects reports instead of exhausting the heap (civ-clone/web-renderer#614)
